The user is playing Monopoly as player p4.

Evaluating whether to buy Mediterranean Avenue or start an auction. The property would complete the brown set for player 3, who already owns Baltic. Previous strategy suggests blocking this purchase without breaking the $600 cash buffer.

Player 3 has $2081 cash and light blue hotels. Completing the brown set would give them a devastating hotel-ready property. Buying Mediterranean for $60 would cost only $459 in cash. The property alone is nearly worthless without Baltic. The decision is whether $60 is worth blocking player 3's brown monopoly.

Player 3 already owns light blue hotels and is the runaway leader with $2081. A brown monopoly would let them build another set cheaply. If I auction, player 3 will almost certainly win it since no one else wants brown. I might still be able to bid in that auction.

I will buy Mediterranean Avenue for $60. This is the cleanest way to block player 3 from completing the brown set. After the purchase, I will have $459 in cash. That leaves me short of the $550–$600 buffer needed for light-blue hotels. I would need to mortgage Park Place, New York Avenue, or the yellow properties to cover that gap.

Recalculating shows buying Mediterranean Avenue for $60 still leaves me solvent. After the purchase I have $459 in cash. Mortgaging Park Place and New York Avenue yields $275, which covers a $600 hotel and leaves me with $134. Even a $550 Vermont hotel is covered by mortgaging just Park Place for $175. I can afford to block player 3's brown monopoly without touching any yellow properties.

Player 3 has $2081 and 9 hotels remaining. They could hotel brown immediately. Mediterranean and Baltic sit on the early board and are frequently landed on after GO. I will buy the property. I may send a brief public message explaining this block.
